name: every-pair-again
why: the nested loops of the starter: correct, and quadratic.

name: no-sort
why: two pointers on data that is not sorted: wrong answers.

name: sorts-the-callers-vector
why: the vector is taken by value from a const_cast: the caller sees it sorted.

edits.old:
std::vector<T> sorted = values;  // sort a COPY: the caller's vector must not change
    std::sort(sorted.begin(), sorted.end());

name: equal-values-counted-as-one-pair
why: when both ends are equal the whole run counts as a single pair.

name: equal-ends-count-m-squared
why: m * m instead of m * (m - 1) / 2: a value is paired with itself.

name: runs-not-multiplied
why: only one pair is counted for a left run and a right run (the product is ignored).

edits.old: pairs += static_cast<long long>(after_left - left) * static_cast<long long>(right - before_right);

name: one-step-on-a-match
why: after a match only one pointer moves: pairs are counted twice or lost.

name: sorts-in-every-step
why: the copy is sorted again on every step of the loop: n log n per step.

edits.new:
std::sort(sorted.begin(), sorted.end());
        const T sum = sorted[left] + sorted[right];

name: copies-the-vector-in-the-loop
why: a fresh copy of the vector for every step.

edits.new:
const std::vector<T> again = sorted;
        const T sum = again[left] + again[right];

name: empty-vector-underflows
why: size() - 1 on an empty vector is a huge unsigned number.
